s3.eventPolicy: first selected-times literal events; remaining events have no output
s3.targetPolicy: retain legal victim; nearest legal substitute after loss

verificationLimits: Native C# ability/FSM dispatcher, particles/audio and frame parity remain unrecovered. Full graphs, source tables and both actual native facing chains are retained.

The S3 table specifies ten slashes but its Front skeleton has eleven identical OnAttack events. Local output uses the first selected-times events (ten) and ignores the eleventh; which event the native dispatcher suppresses is not recovered. No eleven-hit output or evenly spaced replacement clock.

S3 selectTargetTiming2 and refreshInputTargetOnCheckSpell0 are bounded as retaining a legal victim, then selecting its nearest legal substitute if lost. Exact native per-spell retarget/overlap ordering is not executable-recovered.
S2 native primary Physical and extra Arts are independently mitigated. Local Arts-first order is explicit; the original native extra-damage dispatch order is not recovered.

S3 numeric flags3/5 match the original named noirc2_s_1[blockfreeAndInvincible] pair. Immunes0/16 are mapped to Stun/Freeze: inline Ch’en stun confirms0, and Noir’s original cast-state monitor names FROZEN/STUNNED. The compiled enum definition and protection transition frames are not recovered; no broad untargetability or immunity to other control is added.

Source maxAnimScale and literal animation clocks govern local damage; clip completion plus original end-clip is a bounded operation lock. Serialized preDelay/escapeTime are retained rather than added again to OnAttack. Native cooldown/reset/end-state overlap and fractional-tick ordering remain unverified.

Normal double-strike keeps one target and grants one attack SP at first release through the shared engine; exact native SP receipt frame is not recovered. Unborn second hit cancels on accepted control, retirement or skill switch.

Scolding uses source recipient-owned periodic buffs with selected interval/SP, including the owner, and removes them when Ch’en leaves. Native buff-loader zero-phase and simultaneous event priority are not recovered. Blocked SP grants are discarded rather than banked.
Module effects are excluded, consistent with the simulator’s current ordinary-stage support scope.
